newsitem.title: USA: British Air says could reject AMR alliance.
newsitem.headline: British Air says could reject AMR alliance.

text.p: British Airways Plc's Chief Executive Robert Ayling said he remains confident the proposed transatlantic alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines will be approved this summer, but British Air could reject the alliance if regulators required the airlines to pay a burdensome price, such as disposing of a large number of airport slots.

"I do accept that it is perfectly conceivable...that the price that is sought by the competition authorities could be greater than what would be in the interest of our company to agree to," Ayling said.
"If the terms are so penal that they are not in our commercial interest, we will say no," Ayling said.

Ayling said he expects both the alliance and a new Anglo-U.S. air treaty will be approved by the early to mid-summer. American and British Airways have said their alliance remains contingent on the development of a new "open skies" agreement between the two countries.

"We obviously would like it (the alliance) to be dealt with as expediently as possible, but we don't want that to prevent the right outcome. It's the outcome that matters. And if it takes another month or two months, we can be patient," Ayling said. "I am optimistic that it is more likely than not that we will get an outcome that is satisfactory."
Ayling was speaking at press conference in Manhattan to announce a $100 million expansion of British Air's terminal at John F. Kennedy International Airport.
